title: Security managers: every interpreter check, in the same order
summary: Compiled code makes every security-manager check the interpreter makes: LOCAL and ENVIRONMENT (environment symbols, including the specials), CALL (external routines and functions), COMMAND (RC, ERROR and FAILURE from the manager), STREAM (before a stream opens; the answer is the STREAM entry), METHOD (protected methods) and the CALL checks of INTERPRETed code. The protocol is the interpreter's: the manager must return a result (else error 91.999) that is exactly 0 or 1 (else 34.903); 1 means handled. The fixture native/fixtures/program_constructs/security_manager.rex, run by native/test_program_constructs3.sh, gives output identical to the interpreter, including the order of the manager's calls.
procedure: Which manager applies: an activation takes its package's manager when it starts (rx::ActivationScope::security via securityAtActivationStart). A manager set during a routine applies only to activations started afterwards, not to that routine's own calls.
The package's manager is read from PackageClass and SecurityManager fields found by calibration at library load (packageFields).

Interpreter code run on behalf of compiled code (external calls, commands, delegated built-ins, sends, INTERPRET) runs in helper routines; helperRoutine gives each the activation's manager before every CallRoutine. Machinery helpers (internalRoutine) run with none.
Helpers contain no dot symbol of their own; they use the library's private routines RX2CPP_CALLER_CONTEXT and RX2CPP_TAKE, so the manager sees no request the source did not make.

While a manager is active, rxobj::send to an interpreter object goes through the rx2cpp_secured_send helper so protected methods are checked; cost is one helper call per send, only while a manager is active.
INTERPRET: the code object is made natively and its package given the activation's manager.
invariants: The instance-wide manager of ooRexx 5.3 is never set (InterpreterInstance::setSecurityManager has no callers); there is nothing to support.
Not handled specially: REQUIRES (the interpreter loads packages itself).

Checked identical: a protected method sent by the activation that set the manager is not checked, by a later routine it is (security_same_activation.rex); protected MAKESTRING and = reached by SAY, ||, LENGTH, a comparison and REQUEST are asked about as interpreted (security_internal_sends.rex). About 40 internal API sends of the runtime (CLASS, ID, PACKAGE queries) do not use the secured path; none has been found to differ.
Tom Dyer's projects use security managers extensively: a change that breaks security_manager.rex or env_security.rex is not mergeable.
